sources.name: Deloitte, official website
sources.note: private professional services network; added by the editor 2026-10-01 as an IT services and consulting peer of Kyndryl; no SEC filing

reading.body:
Deloitte is recorded here as an AI services provider, not an AI product company: no products, cases, or MCP servers are listed.

The profile text is the only substantive data. It describes consulting work on AI staffing, AI factory and infrastructure trends, data and governance, and cost concerns including token costs, latency, and sovereignty at scale. The one concrete engagement cited is migrating 3,000 knowledge base articles into a new ITSM system using AI instead of manual work.

For AI scaling, this is a demand-side signal rather than a supply-side one. Deloitte's own material points at the constraints that matter downstream of compute: token costs, latency, and sovereignty, which are the operating limits enterprises hit once models are deployed. The 3,000-article migration is small in compute terms and says nothing about how much power or building capacity such work requires.

What the data does not cover is large. There are no figures on Deloitte's own AI infrastructure, no client names, no dates for the cited work, and no indication of how much of its business depends on AI. The profile is a description of what the firm says about itself, verified on 2026-10-01, and should be read as positioning rather than as evidence of capacity.
